title: Pure hex coordinate library with tests
description: src/hex/ - axial (q,r) storage with cube coordinate math for distance, neighbors, diagonals, line drawing, rings and spirals, plus pointy-top layout conversion between hex and world space and pixel-to-hex rounding. Zero Babylon or Vue imports; this module is the spine every other part of the app consumes.
design: Follow the Red Blob Games hex grid reference. Store axial, compute in cube. Layout is a matrix constant so flat-top can be added later without touching call sites.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover round-trip hex-to-world-to-hex, distance, neighbor ordering, ring and spiral generation, and pixel rounding at hex boundaries; no engine imports in the module.
close_reason: src/hex/ landed: coords + layout + 44 passing tests, typecheck clean

title: Fog of war with sight-radius reveal
description: Unexplored hexes render hidden or dimmed until the party has seen them. Reveal happens within a sight radius around the party and accumulates as the party travels, so the map fills in along the route the players actually walked.
acceptance_criteria: Explored-hex set lives in the store and persists across route changes; hexes within sight radius of the party are revealed; unexplored hexes are visually distinct; reveal logic is unit tested on hex distance.
close_reason: Terrain LOS fog shipped: vision.ts + sight.ts, grid fog layer, store explored/visible, panel controls

title: Party token on the map
description: A party marker occupies one hex and is the anchor for fog reveal and movement. Needs a store-owned party position, a Babylon mesh that sits on the tile's elevation, and re-placement when the party moves along a route.
acceptance_criteria: Party position lives in the hexMap store; a visible marker mesh renders at the party's hex at correct elevation; moving the party updates the mesh; unit tests cover the store transitions.
close_reason: Party pawn mesh + store partyHex/arrive shipped; tests and typecheck green

title: [epic] P2: party, fog, authoring, persistence
description: Second feature wave after the interactive grid + routing epic. Covers the party token and fog of war, live terrain authoring controls, multi-waypoint routes, and map persistence.

title: Elevation-aware route tracing
description: Hexes are 10km across. A player picks a start and an end hex; the app traces the fastest route across the terrain. Moving to a hex at the same or lower elevation costs 10km; climbing to a higher one costs double, so routes should prefer contouring around hills over climbing them.
design: A* lives in src/hex/ as pure coordinate code with a pluggable cost function, so it never imports terrain or Babylon. The travel cost model lives in src/terrain/. Minimum step cost is one hex, so hex distance times 10km is an admissible heuristic and A* returns a genuinely optimal route.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking two hexes highlights the traced route and reports hex count and total km; a route over flat ground costs 10km per step; climbing costs 20km; descending costs 10km; routes detour around climbs when contouring is cheaper; A* cost matches Dijkstra on the same graph.
close_reason: A* pathfinder, 10km/hex travel model with double-cost climbs, route overlay and panel readout

title: Hex picking, hover and selection into Pinia
description: Enable thin instance picking, resolve the picked instance index back to axial coordinates, and emit hover and select events from the engine into a Pinia store. A Vue overlay panel reads the store and displays the selected hex coordinates - proving the engine-to-UI bridge end to end.
design: Engine emits plain data (axial coords), never Babylon objects, so nothing engine-owned enters Vue reactivity. Hover highlight is a color buffer write, not a separate mesh.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering tints a hex; clicking selects it and the axial coords appear in the Vue overlay; picking stays accurate after camera rotation and zoom.
close_reason: Thin-instance grid with beveled tiles, hover/select through Pinia, Perlin terrain; verified in browser

title: Render hex grid with thin instances
description: One hexagonal prism source mesh plus per-tile thin instances carrying transform matrices and a per-instance color buffer, so the whole grid draws in a single call. Naive per-hex mesh cloning collapses around 2k tiles; thin instances hold 10k+. Per-hex elevation is baked into the instance matrix.
design: Instance index maps to axial key via a parallel array so picking can resolve an instance back to a hex. Tile visual state lives in the data model and is pushed to the color buffer, not stored on scene nodes.
acceptance_criteria: 5000+ pointy-top hexes render at 60fps in one draw call; updating a single tile color does not rebuild the whole buffer; elevation offsets show correctly.
close_reason: Thin-instance grid with beveled tiles, hover/select through Pinia, Perlin terrain; verified in browser

title: Isometric orthographic camera rig
description: ArcRotateCamera in ORTHOGRAPHIC_CAMERA mode giving the tabletop axonometric look: beta locked at roughly 55 degrees, alpha snapped to 60-degree increments to match hex 6-fold symmetry, zoom driven by orthoLeft/Right/Top/Bottom rather than radius. Pan via pointer drag with configurable bounds.
design: Zoom must recompute all four ortho planes from a single zoom scalar plus canvas aspect ratio, otherwise the view skews on resize.
acceptance_criteria: Rotation snaps cleanly to six orientations; zoom scales the frustum without perspective distortion; panning moves the target and stays within map bounds; aspect stays correct across resizes.
close_reason: Babylon bootstrap, iso ortho camera rig and controls verified on screen

title: Babylon engine bootstrap + useHexScene composable
description: Mount a Babylon 8 Engine and Scene on a canvas inside a Vue component. Render loop start/stop tied to component lifecycle, ResizeObserver driving engine.resize(), full disposal on unmount. Engine and scene handles held in shallowRef - never reactive(), since Vue proxies around Babylon objects destroy render loop performance.
design: Composable returns { canvasRef, scene, engine, onPick } and owns all lifecycle. Vue components never touch Babylon objects directly; they read state from Pinia instead.
acceptance_criteria: Component mounts a scene with a clear color, resizes with the window, disposes cleanly on unmount with no leaked render loop or WebGL context.
close_reason: Babylon bootstrap, iso ortho camera rig and controls verified on screen

title: Scaffold Vue 3 + TS + Vite project
description: Bun-managed Vite project with Vue 3 SFCs, TypeScript strict mode, vue-router and Pinia installed. Establishes the src/ layout (hex/, engine/, stores/, components/, persistence/) the rest of the milestone fills in.
acceptance_criteria: bun run dev serves a Vue app; bun run build succeeds; tsconfig has strict true; src/ directories exist.
notes: Partially done by the hex-lib work: package.json (bun, type module, test/typecheck scripts), tsconfig.json (strict, bundler resolution), .gitignore already exist. Remaining: Vue 3 + Vite + vue-router + Pinia, index.html, app entry, engine/ stores/ components/ persistence/ dirs.
close_reason: Vue 3 + Vite 8 + router + Pinia scaffold; dev server, build and typecheck all green

title: Wire tooling: eslint, prettier, vitest, typecheck
description: ESLint flat config with vue + typescript plugins, Prettier formatting, Vitest for the hex library unit tests, and a typecheck script. Set up before real code lands so quality gates exist from the first commit.
acceptance_criteria: bun run lint, bun run format, bun run typecheck and bun run test all execute and pass on the scaffold.
notes: vitest 5 and typescript 7 already installed as devDeps with test/test:watch/typecheck scripts wired and green. Remaining: ESLint flat config (vue + ts plugins), Prettier, lint/format scripts.
close_reason: ESLint 10 flat config (js + typescript-eslint + vue + prettier), Prettier with repo style, lint/lint:fix/format/format:check scripts. All four gates green.

title: P0+P1: scaffold + interactive hex grid
description: First milestone: Vue 3 + Babylon 8 toolchain running, pure hex coordinate library with tests, and a pointy-top hex grid rendered via thin instances under an isometric orthographic camera, pickable and selectable. Proves the Babylon/Vue/thin-instance architecture before any editor or session features are built on it.
design: Babylon owns the canvas imperatively; Vue owns DOM overlay UI. Engine handle lives in shallowRef, never reactive() - proxies around meshes break the render loop. Bridge is a useHexScene() composable plus an emitter pushing pick/hover events into Pinia. src/hex/ is pure TS with zero Babylon imports.
acceptance_criteria: Grid of pointy-top hexes renders at 60fps with 5k+ tiles in a single draw call; isometric ortho camera rotates in 60-degree steps and zooms via ortho frustum size; clicking a hex selects it and the axial coords show in a Vue overlay panel; hex lib unit tests pass.
close_reason: All seven children complete: scaffold, hex lib, thin-instance grid, iso camera, picking into Pinia, engine bootstrap, and the lint/format/test/typecheck gates

title: Toggle: draw arrows for the whole logged path, or just the last leg
description: The route arrows only ever show the leg the party is walking or has just walked. Add a toggle that traces the whole journey log instead, so a crawl reads as one continuous trail. Off is the current behaviour. The trail is drawn up to the row the party is standing on and, while a route is still being walked, continues into the revealed stretch of it — so the arrows always form one unbroken line ending at the party rather than jumping across the map. The leg drawn after arrival is already in the log and is not drawn twice. Persisted like the other view toggles.
acceptance_criteria: A toggle switches the arrows between the whole logged path and the last leg; the drawn trail is contiguous in both modes, including after a recall part-way down the log; an animated leg in progress continues the trail rather than being hidden; the setting survives a reload; unit tested.
close_reason: Verified in the browser by the user.

title: Auto travel reveals only the endpoints, not the ground it crossed
description: Exploration accumulates from wherever the party stands, so an animated walk carves a corridor of revealed ground one step at a time. Auto travel never stands anywhere in between: it goes from one end of the leg to the other in a single move, so everything the party walked past stays under fog. The same leg walked at speed 1 and on auto leaves two different maps. Reveal along every hex of a committed leg, not just where it ended up.
acceptance_criteria: A leg walked on auto reveals the same ground as the same leg walked at a speed; the corridor is explored along its whole length; an animated walk is unaffected; unit tested against both speeds.
close_reason: Verified in the browser by the user.

title: Recall rolls the fog back to what was known at that step
description: Clicking a log row already moves the party back to that hex. The map does not follow: ground revealed by the steps being undone stays explored, so winding back leaves the party looking at terrain it has not seen yet from where it now stands. Make the explored set a function of how far down its log each party has actually walked — the union of what every traveler could see from each step up to the one it is standing on — and recompute it on recall. Uses the current sight radius rather than whatever was set at the time, which is the party's eyes as they are now.
acceptance_criteria: Recalling to a step un-explores ground first seen after it; ground seen at or before that step stays explored; walking forward again re-reveals it; every traveler contributes what it has seen up to its own position; unit tested.
close_reason: Verified in the browser by the user.

title: Clear the journey log, and reset it when the party turns off the record
description: Replaces the double-click rewind (hexcrawl_web-9tn.15), which deleted history. The log now keeps everything by default. A 'clear the log' button starts the record again from where the party stands, seeding it with the current position as step zero. Walking on from a hex the party was recalled to either retraces what the log already says, which changes nothing and just advances the party along it, or contradicts it: a leg that leaves the recorded path means the recorded future never happened, so the log is cleared and restarted from the hex the party turned off at, with the new direction as its first steps. Which log entry the party is standing on is tracked as an index, because a crawl can cross the same hex twice.
acceptance_criteria: A clear button empties the log and seeds it with the party's current position at zero km; recalling to a step and re-walking the recorded path leaves the log untouched and moves the party along it; walking past the end of the recorded path appends only the new ground; a leg that diverges clears the log and restarts it from the turn-off hex; the row the party stands on is marked exactly, even when the same hex appears twice; unit tested.
close_reason: Verified in the browser by the user.

title: Rewind the journey by double-clicking a log entry
description: Single-clicking a journey row stands the party back on that hex and leaves the record alone. Double-clicking it winds the journey back for real: the party stands there again and every step it took afterwards is struck from the log. Keyed on the step index rather than the hex, because a crawl can cross the same hex twice and only the row that was clicked should decide where the cut falls. Explored ground is left alone — rewinding where the party is does not un-see the terrain; 'forget the map' is the tool for that.
acceptance_criteria: Double-clicking a journey row moves the party to that step and drops every later step; the clicked step survives; a pending destination is cleared and the drawn path reset; an out-of-range step is refused; explored hexes are untouched; single click stays non-destructive; unit tested.
close_reason: Reverted at the user's request: deleting history was the wrong trade. Superseded by hexcrawl_web-9tn.16, which keeps the log and clears it only on an explicit button or a divergent leg.

title: One click per leg: selection commits the walked route
description: The party needed a 'move party here' button to take up its destination, which made every leg two gestures and let the token fall behind the route. Selection now carries it: the first click puts the party on the map, and each click after that plans the next leg and commits the one before it. Clicking the hex the party stands on calls off the planned leg. A route still mid-animation is being replanned rather than finished, so it commits nothing. The button is gone.
acceptance_criteria: No 'move party here' button; the first click places the party; a later click commits the previous leg and sets the next goal; clicking the party's own hex clears the goal without taking the party off the map; a click during an unfinished animation replans without committing; unit tested.
close_reason: Journey log, one-click legs and log recall landed; auto-arrival regression fixed and verified by the suite.

title: Journey log: record every hex the party walks
description: The map keeps where the party is but not how it got there. Record an ordered log of every hex the party actually travels through, with the cost and terrain of each step, so the session has a readable history of its pathing. The log persists in the SQLite save alongside the rest of the map state, which also pins the party's last position to something the reload can read back rather than infer. Shown in the side panel as a running list. Single party for now; per-traveler logs come with hexcrawl_web-9tn.4.
design: Entries are appended when a journey is committed rather than while the reveal animation runs, so an abandoned half-walked route leaves no false history, and auto mode logs the same hexes as animated mode.
acceptance_criteria: Committing a move appends one entry per hex of the route, in order, with per-step km and terrain; the log survives a reload; total distance travelled is derivable from it; the panel lists the journey; unit and round-trip tested.
close_reason: Journey log, one-click legs and log recall landed; auto-arrival regression fixed and verified by the suite.

title: Reveal animation and fog across chained legs
description: The reveal animation walks a whole waypoint chain rather than one leg, and fog/exploration accumulate along it. With several travelers, exploration is the union of what each has seen.
acceptance_criteria: Play walks every leg of a chain in order without resetting between legs; explored hexes accumulate across the chain; multiple travelers each contribute to the explored set; unit tested.

title: Traveler list UI and multiple party tokens
description: A selectable list panel of travelers and groups, and one token per traveler rendered on the map instead of the single pawn. Selecting a row in the list, or clicking a token, sets what map clicks route. Grouped travelers read as a group in the list.
acceptance_criteria: List shows travelers and groups and drives selection; each traveler renders its own token at its own hex; the selected traveler or group is visually distinct; token instancing is unit tested.

title: Convoy groups: join travelers onto one shared path
description: Travelers can be joined into a named group that walks a single shared route (caravan/convoy), and split back out to walk their own. Selecting the group routes every member together; selecting a member on its own detaches it from the group path.
acceptance_criteria: Travelers join and leave a group; a grouped traveler follows the group route; selecting the group routes all members; splitting a member gives it an independent route; group membership is unit tested.

title: Multi-leg routes: waypoint chain with per-leg and total km
description: A traveler's route becomes an ordered chain of waypoints rather than a single start/goal pair. Appending a waypoint adds a leg from the last one; removing a waypoint re-stitches the chain. Distance is reported per leg and as a chain total.
acceptance_criteria: Waypoints append and remove; the route chains legs in order through findRoute; per-leg km and total km are exposed by the store and shown in the UI; unit tested including empty, single and many-leg chains.

title: Traveler model and store: list, add, remove, select
description: Introduce a Traveler entity (id, name, colour, position hex) and hold an ordered list of them in the hexMap store, replacing the single implicit party. Travelers can be added, removed and renamed, and exactly one traveler or group is the current selection that map clicks act on. The existing single-party behaviour becomes one traveler in the list so nothing regresses.
acceptance_criteria: Store exposes travelers, selection, add/remove/rename/select actions; the current party token is one traveler in the list; existing party/route behaviour is unchanged for a single traveler; unit tested.
close_reason: Verified in the browser by the user.

title: Relief slider changed nothing: matrix instance buffer was static
description: The grid created its thin-instance matrix buffer with staticBuffer=true, from when tile heights were written once at build time. Live terrain controls rewrite those matrices, but a static buffer cannot be re-uploaded, so thinInstanceBufferUpdated('matrix') never reached the GPU. Colours used a non-static buffer and did update, which is why sea level looked half-alive while relief looked dead. Verified with a probe: staticBuffer=true leaves world0 and matrixBuffer isUpdatable()=false.
acceptance_criteria: Both instance buffers are updatable and a regression test asserts it.
close_reason: Matrix buffer created non-static; regression test asserts world0 and instanceColor stay updatable

title: Reserve the sight bonus for mountains and peaks
description: Every step up currently widens the sight radius, so walking from a beach into grass or forest already buys extra reach. Only real high ground should: keep the bonus for the top two bands and rename rock and snow to mountains and peaks while the terrain vocabulary is being settled.
acceptance_criteria: Water, sand, grass and forest all see the same distance; mountains and peaks each add reach; the terrain ids read mountains and peaks throughout.
close_reason: vantageFloor gates the sight bonus above the treeline; rock and snow renamed to mountains and peaks

title: Only ground above the party blocks its view
description: Line of sight is pure slope maths, so a ridge below the party still casts a shadow into the ground past it. Standing on a height should mean seeing over everything lower: only a hex on a step above the party can get in the way, and the slope test then decides how far its shadow reaches.
acceptance_criteria: A hex at or below the party's level never blocks; a hex above it blocks by the existing slope test; looking down from a summit clears the whole disc; existing ridge and peak behaviour from lower ground is unchanged.
close_reason: Only hexes on a step above the party contribute a blocking claim; the slope test then decides how far that shadow reaches

title: Split elevation into mechanical levels and rendered height
description: Line of sight, blocking and climb cost all read the continuous rendered height, so mechanics turn on differences too small to see and the climb threshold never fires. Give every tile an integer level for mechanics and keep the smooth height for rendering, then spread the rendered range further apart for more contrast in the terrain.
acceptance_criteria: TerrainTile carries an integer level alongside its rendered elevation; LOS and climb cost read the level; rendering reads the height; the rendered range is visibly taller and level order matches height order.
close_reason: TerrainTile carries a band-pinned integer level; LOS and climb cost read it, rendering keeps the smooth height. Climb share on generated terrain went from inert to 12.3% of adjacent steps.

title: Pinia store survives HMR and crashes reloaded components
description: hexMap.ts never called acceptHMRUpdate, so the live store instance outlived every hot update. A component hot-reloading against a store that had since grown a field crashed on it — hit while adding blocked to the sight field, where HexCanvas threw 'store.blocked is not iterable' against a stale store.
acceptance_criteria: Editing the store hot-updates its instance instead of leaving a stale one behind.
close_reason: Wired acceptHMRUpdate in hexMap.ts

title: Sight field overlay showing what the terrain blocks
description: Fog shows where the party has been but not why it cannot see further. A toggle draws the sight disc as translucent plates over the terrain: cool glaze on hexes in line of sight, red shade on hexes within reach that something is standing in front of, so a ridge reads as the shadow it casts.
acceptance_criteria: Panel toggle turns the overlay on and off; plates are translucent and sit over the terrain they describe; blocked hexes inside the sight radius are visually distinct from visible ones; vision reports blocked hexes and the whole path is unit tested.
close_reason: Sight overlay shipped: fieldOfView reports blocked hexes, visionOverlay draws translucent lit/shadow plates, panel toggle

title: Persist map state to a local SQLite DB
description: src/persistence/ is empty. Stand up a browser-local SQLite database (sqlite-wasm, OPFS sahpool VFS) as the save layer, and cover the state that already exists: terrain controls (seed, scale, seaLevel, relief), route endpoints, explored-hex set, sight radius, fog/showSight/allowWater flags. Terrain tiles are NOT stored — they are derived from seed + controls. First pass only; the schema is expected to be refined once travelers and groups land (see hexcrawl_web-9tn.4).
design: sqlite-wasm over localStorage because the sandbox is heading for a shared live session and a real relational schema now maps onto a server DB later. OPFS sahpool VFS avoids needing COOP/COEP headers. Tests open :memory: so they exercise the same SQL.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned SQLite schema opens in the browser and persists across reload; save/load round-trips every store field listed above; loading restores terrain, route endpoints and explored hexes; schema version is recorded and checked; round-trip is integration tested against a real in-memory SQLite.
close_reason: Verified in the browser: OPFS-backed SQLite restores terrain, endpoints and explored hexes across a reload.

title: Travelers: selectable parties, convoy groups, multi-leg routes
description: Today the map has one implicit party and a single start/goal pair. Replace that with a list of traveler objects. Travelers can be selected from a list; several can be joined into a group (caravan/convoy) that shares one path, or split off to walk routes of their own. Each traveler's route is a chain of waypoints with per-leg and total distance. Selecting a group routes the whole group; selecting a single traveler reroutes just that one. Broken into children.
acceptance_criteria: Parent is done when all children are closed.

title: Live terrain controls: seed, scale, sea level, relief
description: Terrain options are currently code-only defaults. Expose seed, scale, sea level and relief in the side panel so maps can be tuned in the browser and regenerated without an edit-reload cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Panel exposes seed/scale/seaLevel/relief; changing a value regenerates terrain and refreshes the scene; route and party state react sensibly to regeneration.
close_reason: Panel exposes seed/scale/seaLevel/relief; grid re-terrains in place via HexGrid.setTiles so the camera, party and fog survive a regenerate

title: Climb threshold makes elevation inert on generated terrain
description: stepCostKm now doubles only when the next hex is at least 2 units higher, which correctly stops a party being charged double to wade ashore. But neighbouring hexes on the generated map differ by 0.39 units at the median and 2.05 at the absolute maximum, so only 2 of 29040 adjacent steps qualify. Every route now costs exactly the flat distance and terrain no longer deflects travel at all. Either the threshold drops to around 0.75-1, or terrain relief rises so neighbouring hexes differ more sharply.
acceptance_criteria: A meaningful share of uphill steps cost double, and routes measurably prefer contouring over climbing on the default map
close_reason: TerrainTile carries a band-pinned integer level; LOS and climb cost read it, rendering keeps the smooth height. Climb share on generated terrain went from inert to 12.3% of adjacent steps.

title: Direction arrows along the route
description: Colouring hexes showed the route but not which way it ran. Thin-instanced 3D arrows sit on the seam between consecutive hexes, pointing in the direction of travel, with rounded top edges and a slow hover cycle.
acceptance_criteria: One arrow per step centred on the gap, yawed to travel direction, clearing the taller hex, not pickable, bobbing in a loop
close_reason: Shipped and verified in browser; covered by tests

title: Animated route reveal
description: A traced route appeared instantly, with no sense of travel. A speed slider (auto, 1x, 2x, 3x) plus a start button walks the route hex by hex, counting hexes and kilometres as it goes.
acceptance_criteria: Slider and start button in the panel; reveal paced by requestAnimationFrame; rewinds on route or speed change; auto behaves as before
close_reason: Shipped and verified in browser; covered by tests

title: More pronounced terrain relief
description: Peaks read too flat against the hex size. Terrain relief raised 30 percent, leaving sea level and shoreline heights untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Peak elevation 4.47 to 5.67 units; water and shore unchanged
close_reason: Shipped and verified in browser; covered by tests

title: Zoom-linked camera tilt
description: The isometric tilt was fixed at 54.7 degrees. Tilt now tracks zoom so the view drops toward the horizon up close and flattens to a map view pulled back.
acceptance_criteria: Tilt swings between 15 and 49 degrees above the horizon across the zoom 10-20 band, log interpolated, pinned outside it
close_reason: Shipped and verified in browser; covered by tests

title: Land-only pathfinding toggle
description: Routes crossed open water freely because water is flat and cheap. A toggle in the map panel controls whether the pathfinder may cross water; off by default, since a party on foot cannot swim.
acceptance_criteria: Toggle wired to the route; water impassable by default; endpoints on water rejected when off
close_reason: Shipped and verified in browser; covered by tests

title: Create GitHub repo + README + gh PATH
description: Bootstrap hexcrawl_web: add README.md, create private GitHub repo as origin, push initial commit, and add GitHub CLI to user PATH so 'gh' resolves in all shells.
close_reason: README added, private repo created and pushed, gh added to user PATH

title: Stand the party back on a hex from the journey log
description: The journey list is readable but inert. Clicking a row puts the party back on that hex, so a session can be wound back to where something happened. The log itself is left alone: it records where the party has been, not where it is.
design: Non-destructive on purpose. Truncating the log at the recalled step is the other reading and is easy to add later, but it throws away history the user did not ask to lose.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a journey row sets the party position to that hex and clears any planned leg; the log is unchanged by the recall; a hex that is not in the log is refused; the row the party stands on is marked; unit tested.
close_reason: Journey log, one-click legs and log recall landed; auto-arrival regression fixed and verified by the suite.

title: Extend the SQLite schema to travelers, groups and routes
description: Follow-up to hexcrawl_web-9tn.5: the first persistence pass stores a single party and one route. Once travelers, groups and waypoint chains exist, migrate the schema to store them as proper tables and bump the schema version.
acceptance_criteria: Travelers, group membership and per-traveler waypoint chains persist across reload; a saved DB from the earlier schema version migrates forward; migration is integration tested.

title: Measure and trim the cost of a fog recompute
description: Every party step walks a hex line per target hex, roughly O(radius^3), and then rebuilds a fog map covering the whole board. Fine at a 40-hex radius and three steps per second, but both scale badly. Measure before optimising; shadowcasting would replace the per-target line walk if it turns out to matter.
acceptance_criteria: Cost of one visible/fog recompute is measured at full map size and a high sight radius; a decision is recorded on whether shadowcasting or an incremental fog diff is worth it.

title: Flatten unexplored hexes so fog does not leak elevation
description: Fogged tiles keep their real prism height, so mountains still poke out of ground nobody has seen and their silhouette gives away terrain the fog is meant to hide. Flattening unexplored tiles means rewriting their instance matrices, which the grid currently uploads once at build time.
acceptance_criteria: Unexplored hexes render at a flat height; explored and visible hexes keep their terrain height; the matrix buffer updates without rebuilding the grid.

title: Decide how boats and water travel work
description: Water is currently all-or-nothing: impassable, or the same 10km per hex as land. A hexcrawl probably wants boats, coastal versus open sea, or a distinct water speed. Needs a rules decision before the travel model hardens.
acceptance_criteria: Water travel rules decided and reflected in stepCostKm

title: Measure hover picking cost at full map size
description: Hover runs scene.pick on every pointer move against roughly 5000 thin instances. It has never been profiled. If it costs more than a millisecond or two per move, replace it with a ray-plane intersection against y=0 plus worldToHex, which is O(1) and uses the already-tested hex library.
acceptance_criteria: Pointer-move pick cost measured at radius 40; either confirmed acceptable or replaced with the ground-plane approach

title: Trim the Babylon bundle
description: The production bundle is 1.09 MB, 270 kB gzipped, most of it Babylon's StandardMaterial shader set. Worth checking whether a lighter material or a narrower set of side-effect imports cuts it materially before the app grows.
acceptance_criteria: Bundle size measured per dependency and either reduced or documented as acceptable
